objectives.text: Turn the outer islands into investment without giving up control of them. A long-term lease of about 100 acres on Assomption went to a Qatari company to build a luxury hotel and rebuild an airstrip for international flights. Activists sued over it a week before the 2025 first round, and critics said it favours foreign interests over Seychelles' welfare and sovereignty.

grand_strategy.reading: Seychelles has no treaty ally and keeps several partners at once: India for coast-guard and maritime security, China for the Belt and Road and its fifty years of ties, the United States and the United Kingdom for security and economic partnership, and Qatari capital for a hotel on Assomption. The 2025 runoff, won by Patrick Herminie, was fought partly over a lease that critics said favoured foreign interests, and his government has since pursued the Indian, Chinese and American files at once. Every partner meets the same veto: a foreign base stalled in 2018 under public fears for sovereignty, and the Assomption lease shows that foreign money in the islands carries the same cost.

stances.note: Transactional partner, no treaty. The Assumption Island base planned in 2018 was never built: the amended agreement of January 2018 was never ratified, and sources disagree on whether the government withdrew it or the opposition blocked it. Indian coastal radar (announced 2022) and the defence and technology agreements of the June 2026 state visit are the working ties. Trend warming: the 2026 visit is the strongest signal. One situation report says Ramkalawan had overseen a cooling of ties with India; that cooling is not confirmed by any primary source read here. Bond none: no kinship, and the 2018 base met a public backlash about sovereignty and Indian workers, which is distance, not grievance. Confidence C: the official visit page was seen only as a search result title, the agreements come from press, and the 2018 history is from press snippets.
